review.alternative: Belief processes might converge to a path-independent equilibrium if strong correcting feedback loops are present.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration of complete path independence across diverse misspecified model initializations.

claims.statement: Inferential error and belief updating in preference processes are generally path-dependent under model misspecification.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that inference and belief updating decompose into path-dependent components under model misspecification.
support.passage: inferential error, of a given belief process vs another (e.g. true probability), is in general not path-independent (not round-tripping despite the given belief process doing so); it decomposes uniquely into twoindependentcompo- nents, one path-independent, systematic and identifiable as a well-known behavioural bias, one path-dependent and not necessarily systematic.

actions.findings: Inferential error and belief updating in preference processes are generally path-dependent under model misspecification. [source-0f17f7655d614a90]
actions.limitations: Empirical validation remains restricted to specific binary inference configurations and misspecified model regimes.
actions.next_questions: How do path-dependent components interact with multi-agent preference aggregation over longer horizons?
